examples.question_text: $X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(7,0.4)$. Find $P(X=3)$, correct to four decimal places.
A basketball player scores each shot with probability $0.2$, independently of her other shots. She takes $10$ shots. Find the probability that she scores exactly $2$, correct to four decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Success: she scores a shot. Let $X$ count the shots she scores.
$X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(10,0.2)$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X=2)&={}^{10}C_{2}(0.2)^2(0.8)^8\\&=45\times0.04\times0.16777216\\&=0.301989888\\&\approx0.3020\end{aligned}$

(a) No successes means four failures.
$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&={}^{4}C_{0}(0.7)^0(0.3)^4\\&=1\times1\times(0.3)^4\\&=0.0081\end{aligned}$
(b) Four successes means no failures.
$\begin{aligned}P(X=4)&={}^{4}C_{4}(0.7)^4(0.3)^0\\&=1\times(0.7)^4\times1\\&=0.2401\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A biased coin shows a head with probability $\frac13$, independently on each toss. It is tossed $5$ times. Find the probability of exactly $2$ heads as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
examples.solution_text:
Success: the coin shows a head. Let $X$ count the heads.
$X\sim\mathrm{Bin}\left(5,\frac13\right)$.
$\begin{aligned}P(X=2)&={}^{5}C_{2}\left(\frac13\right)^2\left(\frac23\right)^3\\&=10\times\frac19\times\frac8{27}\\&=\frac{80}{243}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Independently calculated C(7,3)=35, 0.4^3=0.064 and 0.6^4=0.1296. Their product is 0.290304, giving 0.2903 to four decimal places.
The independent shots give X~Bin(10,0.2). Independently calculated C(10,2)=45 and 0.8^8=0.16777216. Thus P(X=2)=45(0.04)(0.16777216)=0.301989888, giving 0.3020 to four decimal places.
For zero successes, C(4,0)=1 and 0.7^0=1, so P(X=0)=0.3^4=0.0081. For four successes, C(4,4)=1 and 0.3^0=1, so P(X=4)=0.7^4=0.2401.
The independent tosses give X~Bin(5,1/3). Independently calculated P(X=2)=C(5,2)(1/3)^2(2/3)^3=10(1/9)(8/27)=80/243. Since 80 has no factor of 3, the fraction is in lowest terms.
